key_insight: TRACE-ROUTER reframes LLM routing for agentic AI as a task-level decision problem, rather than optimizing each call in isolation. This lets the router adapt to delayed feedback and choose models that better balance quality and cost across long-horizon workflows.
problem_solved: Existing LLM routers make independent per-call choices, but agentic applications are multi-step workflows where success is only known after the full task completes. This creates a credit-assignment problem: it is hard to tell which routing decisions helped or hurt the final outcome.
method: Uses task-consistent routing so decisions are optimized for the final workflow outcome, not just immediate call-level signals.
Adapts online to feedback from completed agentic tasks, enabling continual improvement as workloads change.
Balances cost and quality by routing different steps to different LLMs based on learned task-level utility.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this approach can improve the reliability and efficiency of agentic systems that use multiple models across long workflows. It is especially useful in enterprise settings where minimizing cost without sacrificing task success is critical.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing a multi-step agent workflow with routing decisions at each step
Comparison chart of per-call routing vs task-consistent routing
Feedback loop graphic illustrating delayed task-level reward and online adaptation
Cost-quality trade-off plot with different LLMs and routing choices
paper_title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI
paper_authors: Ritik Raj, Souvik Kundu, Sarbartha Banerjee, Dheemanth Joshi, Ishita Vohra
